papers.title: Enabling Rapid Calibration of BCI Systems that Detect Movement-Related Cortical Potentials in Children with Cerebral Palsy.
papers.summary: Developed a Bi-LSTM deep-learning framework for detecting movement-related cortical potentials during ankle dorsiflexion in four children with cerebral palsy across 27 EEG sessions. Cross-subject cumulative learning reached 91% accuracy without within-session calibration, and adding transfer learning raised accuracy to 93% with minimal calibration, outperforming conventional strategies.

papers.title: Bayesian nonparametric identification of spectrally distinct neural states
papers.summary: Proposes a Bayesian nonparametric method combining time-delay embedding with a Dirichlet-process Gaussian mixture model to identify spectrally distinct neural oscillatory states while inferring the number of states from data. Benchmarked on synthetic data and applied to resting-state MEG, the method reliably recovered multiple frequency components under 1/f-like noise and revealed multiple short-lived frequency-selective and aperiodic states with substantial inter-individual heterogeneity.

papers.title: Feature processing for single-trial semantic decoding from EEG: a factorial comparison with pre-registered replication
papers.summary: A factorial comparison of 640 feature-processing configurations for single-trial EEG semantic decoding across three tasks showed that signal representation had the largest effect: waveform features achieved 56.6% balanced accuracy versus 50.6% for theta-band power, and adding band power to waveform reduced accuracy by 1.8 percentage points; these effects replicated and were larger in a pre-registered study of 283 new participants.

papers.title: High-Density EEG Signatures of Cataplexy in Narcolepsy Type 1.
papers.summary: Used 128-channel EEG polysomnography in 10 drug-free adults with narcolepsy type 1 to characterize the electrophysiological signature of 73 cataplexy epochs versus wake, N1, and REM states. Cataplexy showed a distinct hybrid EEG profile with intermediate sleep-wake spectral features and mixed wake/REM/N1 hypnodensity probabilities, differing from direct-entry REM sleep.

papers.title: Integrating convolutional variational autoencoders and the Gaussian mixture model for efficient manifold learning and clustering of spatially preserved EEG topographic maps.
papers.summary: The authors developed Conv-VaDE, a convolutional variational deep embedding model with a Gaussian mixture prior for clustering spatially preserved EEG topographic maps into microstates, and on LEMON resting-state data it produced a reproducible latent manifold (silhouette 0.232) with probabilistic soft assignments and decodable cluster centers, while modified k-means retained higher silhouette and 4-5 percentage points higher global explained variance.

papers.title: Transcranial temporal interference stimulation increases slow waves during human NREM sleep
papers.summary: In 32 participants receiving 1 Hz transcranial temporal interference stimulation (tTIS) and 11 carrier-only controls during NREM sleep, tTIS increased slow-wave density by about 20% during and 30% after stimulation, and stronger modeled electric fields were associated with greater shifts toward N3 sleep.

papers.title: Cross-domain competition for memory reactivation resources during sleep
papers.summary: In a within-subject nap study with 24 participants, targeted memory reactivation cues for an object sequence task disrupted object memory consolidation without indirectly improving a linked motor task, and sleep EEG indicated that slow oscillation and spindle activity were preferentially allocated to the motor trace, suggesting cross-domain competition for reactivation resources.

papers.title: Characterizing the heterogeneity of Alzheimer's disease through EEG normative modeling.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Applying sex-specific EEG normative models of small-world network architecture to 160 AD, 161 MCI, and 769 healthy controls identified two robust EEG-defined subtypes across the AD spectrum, with subtype-1 showing relatively preserved network organization and subtype-2 showing widespread disruption and poorer clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Automated action potential parameter analysis for reproducible electrophysiological measurements in neurons.
papers.summary: The authors developed APpar, a freely available open-source tool for Origin/OriginPro that automatically detects action potentials and extracts a comprehensive set of excitability parameters, including a novel TRUE-threshold validation algorithm to improve consistency of derivative-based threshold detection. Validation using dorsal root ganglion neuron recordings showed stable measurements from identical copied APs and successful extraction of dynamic parameter changes across repetitive and spontaneous firing sequences.

papers.title: A Neuro-Inspired Dual-Pathway Attention Network for EEG-Based Identity Recognition.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The authors propose a dual-pathway attention network for EEG-based identity recognition that separates bottom-up perceptual feature extraction from top-down prior-guided modulation, fused by a quality-aware gate based on instantaneous signal stability. The method achieved 93.8% accuracy on DEAP (5.3 percentage points above the best baseline) and 97.2% on THU-EP, with only 2.5% and 5.2% performance drops in cross-session tests on noisy SEED-IV and 76.8% accuracy with only 1% of training data on THU-EP.

papers.title: EEG biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases: Machine learning applications and clinical trial insights.
papers.summary: This review synthesized evidence from 226 studies on EEG-based biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases, mapping diagnosis, prognosis, treatment monitoring, and patient stratification. It reports spectral power, event-related potentials, and connectivity as main features, with support vector machines and neural networks as primary classifiers, while noting challenges of small samples, methodological heterogeneity, limited interpretability, and gaps in clinical validation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled quality assurance for point-of-care electroencephalographic cap placement by inexperienced users.
papers.summary: In a prospective randomized crossover validation study with 30 participants and 60 placement trials, the authors developed and tested an AI-enabled tool for quality assurance of EEG cap placement by inexperienced users compared with expert technologist placement. Mean absolute positioning error was 0.938 cm with app guidance versus 0.855 cm with expert placement, demonstrating noninferiority against a prespecified 0.5-cm margin, with clinically acceptable placement achieved in 93.3% of app-guided versus 100% of expert trials.

papers.title: Treadmill Walking Differentially Modulates Early Auditory Responses to Standard and Deviant Sounds.
papers.summary: The authors recorded 32-channel EEG from 22 healthy young adults during a passive auditory frequency-oddball paradigm while sitting and treadmill walking with or without carrying cups, examining standard- and deviant-evoked responses in the N1 and mismatch-negativity windows. A significant stimulus-type by movement-condition interaction occurred 80-130 ms after sound onset, with the deviant-evoked response attenuated during walking whereas the standard-evoked response did not differ significantly between conditions.

papers.title: Frontoparietal Hyperconnectivity as a Single-Subject Neural Signature of Chronic Tinnitus
papers.summary: In a multi-site case-control study of 544 participants, normative modeling of resting-state EEG deviations detected chronic tinnitus with AUC 0.832 under site-grouped cross-validation. The most discriminative, site-robust feature was theta-band right orbitofrontal connectivity dominating frontoparietal and dorsal attention networks, supporting a failed top-down gating account.

papers.title: EEG Source Localization with High-Resolution 40-Tissue Head Models: A Comparative Study with MEG during Photic Driving
papers.summary: The authors present a pipeline using the boundary element fast multipole method to compute EEG leadfields on high-resolution 40-tissue head models and applied it to six participants during photic driving, comparing 61-channel EEG source localizations from 40-tissue and 5-layer models with each other and with simultaneously recorded MEG. The two models produced highly consistent EEG source localizations (weighted relative difference below 3%), both in close agreement with MEG localizations within the visual cortex, establishing 40-tissue models as a practical and robust basis for EEG source localization.

papers.title: Childhood emotional neglect modulates emotional face processing in healthy young adults: An ERP study.
papers.summary: In 54 healthy young adults performing an emotional face categorization task with 32-channel EEG, childhood emotional neglect (but not emotional abuse) was associated with increased P100 amplitude across expressions, shorter N170 latency, and an EN × valence interaction on LPP amplitude and reaction times. These preliminary findings link emotional neglect to altered early and late stages of emotional face processing in a non-clinical sample.

papers.title: Preparatory beta activity reflects the precision demands of an upcoming movement
papers.summary: EEG recorded in 27 healthy adults preparing reaches to narrow versus wide targets showed lower preparatory beta power (13–30 Hz) over bilateral parieto-occipital electrodes for narrow, higher-precision targets, with no alpha or theta differences. Narrow targets also produced more precise movements, greater muscle co-activation, and larger long-latency perturbation responses, indicating preparatory beta reflects task precision demands.

papers.title: How Perceived Traits Modulate the Neural Processing of Reward During Reinforcement Learning.
papers.summary: Using reinforcement learning models to separate reward and generosity prediction errors alongside EEG, the study found that positive reward prediction errors elicited larger reward positivity, stronger delta power, and reduced N400 amplitudes than negative reward prediction errors only when generosity prediction errors were negative. Perceived trait learning thus asymmetrically modulates reward salience and evaluation during learning.

papers.title: Late cortical dynamics mediate numerosity illusions induced by symmetry.
papers.summary: EEG with univariate and multivariate analyses showed that physical numerosity was decodable from occipitoparietal electrodes as early as ~50 ms, while spatial arrangement and symmetry-biased perceived numerosity emerged later around ~150 ms. The results indicate early direct encoding of physical numerosity and late grouping processes underlying the symmetry-induced underestimation illusion.

papers.title: Interrater agreement of seizure onset and spread in scalp EEG
papers.summary: Three epileptologists independently annotated onset and contralateral spread channels and timing for 79 seizures from 48 presurgical patients, yielding substantial onset laterality agreement (Gwet k=0.73) and comparable spread-presence agreement (0.63), but lower channel-level agreement for spread (Cohen k=0.38) versus onset (0.57). The authors release a multi-expert annotated dataset as a reference standard for automated spread detection.

papers.title: Association of the 2HELPS2B Score With Impaired Recovery of Consciousness and In-Hospital Mortality in Critically Ill Patients: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
papers.summary: This multicenter retrospective study of 33 critically ill adults with persistent impaired consciousness examined whether a 2HELPS2B score of 2 or higher was associated with failure to improve FOUR score and in-hospital mortality. High scores were associated with failure to improve FOUR score (44.4% vs 4.2%; crude RR 10.67) but not significantly with mortality, in a small unadjusted cohort.

papers.title: An investigation into the cognitive influences on caloric-induced cortical alpha suppression and vestibular responsiveness.
papers.summary: Examined how cognitive tasking (mental arithmetic) influences caloric-induced cortical alpha suppression and its relationship to peak slow-phase velocity (pSPV) using EEG and electronystagmography in 20 healthy adults. Tasking produced the largest global reduction in cortical alpha suppression (p < 0.001) and increased pSPV (p = 0.033), but individual changes in periodic alpha features and the aperiodic exponent were not associated with pSPV changes (p > 0.05), suggesting independent mechanisms for cortical activity and vestibulo-ocular reflex output.

papers.title: Shared Neural Dynamics of Sentence-Level Language Processing in Verbally Proficient Autistic and Non-Autistic Adults
papers.summary: Using EEG during rapid serial visual presentation of sentences and pseudoword lists, the authors compared verbally proficient autistic and non-autistic adults and found comparable oscillatory responses across theta, alpha, beta, and gamma bands, with beta-band activity increasing over sentence position and correlating with verbal ability. The results indicate largely shared neural dynamics of sentence-level language processing in both groups.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in epilepsy care: a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical applications in diagnosis, classification, outcome prediction, and surgical decision-making.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis pooled 102 studies of AI/ML in epilepsy and found strong discriminative performance across clinical tasks, with the highest pooled AUC for etiological classification (0.929), followed by diagnosis (0.899), surgical referral (0.895), and outcome prediction (0.807), alongside high risk of bias and scarce external validation. Sensitivity was lowest for surgical referral (0.729), highlighting a clinically relevant asymmetry.

papers.title: Direct cortical electrical stimulation-induced seizures: Are they reliable? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 25 studies found stimulation-induced seizures occurred more often with high-frequency than low-frequency stimulation (56.1% vs 35.8%; OR 1.83), but SIS frequency itself was not linked to favorable postoperative outcome. Instead, the proportion of habitual electro-clinical seizures among SIS correlated with better Engel Ia outcomes under low-frequency stimulation, emphasizing semiological and EEG concordance over SIS occurrence.

papers.title: Label-Free Live Cell Type Prediction by Integrating Raman Spectroscopy and Machine Learning.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using coherent Raman spectroscopy combined with a shallow XGBoost classifier, the authors profiled 286 live single cells from patient-derived glioma lines and distinguished IDH1-mutant from IDH1-wild-type cells (ROC-AUC 0.78) and IDH1-mutant astrocytoma from oligodendroglioma (ROC-AUC 0.81). Feature importance implicated protein amide bands, NADH, unsaturated fatty acids, heme-related modes, and lipid-rich vesicle signatures in the separations.

papers.title: Multifunctional CNT-based Platform for Enhanced Dopaminergic Differentiation and Electrochemical Dopamine Sensing from Human iPSC-derived Neurons.
papers.summary: The authors developed a carbon nanotube-based electroactive platform combining human iPSC-derived neurons with CNTs, which enhanced the electroactive area, catalyzed dopamine oxidation, and promoted dopaminergic differentiation (TH/neurofilament overlap 37.90% vs 26.01% in controls). Using differential pulse voltammetry and chronoamperometry, they quantified extracellular dopamine release at 1.25 µM and confirmed stimulus-dependent release after benztropine and KCl depolarization.

papers.title: Seizure Freedom After Focal Epilepsy Surgery in a Child With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex and Coexisting Suspected Subependymal Giant Cell Astrocytoma: A Case Report.
papers.summary: A case report of a 3-year-old girl with tuberous sclerosis complex and drug-resistant focal epilepsy who became clinically seizure-free for 18 months after neuronavigation-guided left frontal resection, with emergence of independent walking and syllabic speech despite persistent epileptiform EEG activity.

papers.title: EEG and fNIRS evidence for brain responses to three tannins: implications for astringency surface sub-quality in red wine.
papers.summary: Used EEG, fNIRS, sensory analysis, LC-MS and molecular docking to compare brain and sensory responses to tannic acid, grape tannin, and wine tannin matched for astringency intensity. The three tannins evoked distinct frontal cortical activation (notably ventromedial prefrontal channel 6) and sensory responses ranked wine tannin > tannic acid > grape tannin, with finer astringency linked to higher tannin oligomers, polymeric pigments, and free anthocyanins.

papers.title: Intranasal embelin-nanostructured lipid carrier with β-cyclodextrin inclusion complex (EBCD) produces sustained behavioural control of convulsive activity in the lithium-pilocarpine rat model: A behavioural and neurochemical comparison with intranasal diazepam.
papers.summary: Tested an intranasal embelin-β-cyclodextrin nanostructured lipid carrier (EBCD) against intranasal diazepam in the lithium-pilocarpine rat model of status epilepticus, with treatment withheld until convulsive activity was confirmed. Both treatments produced sustained seizure control in all animals versus none of untreated controls, and both reduced elevated hippocampal glutamate, though the study was not powered to establish non-inferiority.

papers.title: Machine learning-assisted fusion of urinary Raman and fluorescence spectra for detection of urothelial carcinoma.
papers.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
papers.summary: Combined fiber-optic Raman and UV/VIS-excited fluorescence spectroscopy of unprocessed urine with machine learning to detect urothelial carcinoma in 285 patients (120 cases, 165 controls). A PCA-LDA fusion model reached only ~64% accuracy, whereas an artificial neural network on full spectral data with augmentation exceeded 90% accuracy.

papers.title: The mechanism of regulation of prokaryotic Na+ channels by their C-terminal domain
papers.summary: Combined electrophysiology and computational modeling to show that the cytoplasmic C-terminal domain of the prokaryotic Na+ channel NaVSp1 is not itself a temperature sensor but is conformationally coupled to pore gating. CTD-transmembrane interactions stabilize the open state and can reduce or abolish temperature sensitivity, and modeling of >800 bacterial sequences suggests this architecture is broadly conserved across BacNaV channels.

papers.title: Myosin II-FAK-paxillin Signaling Governs Mechanosensitive Responses of Neuronal Cells to Magnetic Stimulation
papers.summary: Characterized mechanotransduction downstream of magnetic stimulation in N27-A dopaminergic cells using DNA-based integrin tension sensors and pharmacological manipulation. Magnetic stimulation increased integrin tension in a dose-, frequency-, and pulse-number-dependent manner via a myosin II- and FAK-dependent pathway, producing more internal adhesions with increased phosphorylated paxillin.

papers.title: MiR-182 regulates IL-6 and HCN4 in the cardiac context: implications for human atrial electrical remodelling.
papers.summary: Using hiPS-CM overexpression, zebrafish models, and human atrial biopsies, this study shows that miR-182 overexpression reduces irregular spontaneous beating, downregulates the pacemaker channel HCN4, and increases IL-6 expression and secretion; miR-182-5p was elevated in left atrial dilation and permanent AF biopsies and correlated positively with IL-6.

papers.title: A synaptic mitochondrion-ribbon-vesicle complex organizes photoreceptor neurotransmission.
papers.summary: Combining FIB-SEM and electrophysiology, this study shows that photoreceptor synapses organize mitochondria, ribbons, and vesicles into synaptic mitochondrion-ribbon-vesicle complexes (sMRVcs) with a strict 1:1 rod architecture versus multiple distributed cone units; disrupting syntaphilin altered rod mitochondria-ribbon ratios and enhanced transmission, and sMRVcs disassembled before functional decline in retinal degeneration.

papers.title: An apparently de novo UBE3A missense variant p.(Tyr777Cys) in the HECT domain in a child with an atypical early childhood phenotype suggestive of Angelman syndrome: a case report and focused literature review.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 30-month-old boy with global developmental delay, severe expressive language impairment, EEG abnormalities, and delayed myelination who carries an apparently de novo UBE3A HECT-domain missense variant p.(Tyr777Cys) classified as a variant of uncertain significance, with a focused literature review.

papers.title: Membrane Lipid Composition and Asymmetry Modulate Translocation Versus Leakage of the Model Amphipathic Peptide MAP.
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: Using high-field computational electrophysiology simulations benchmarked by liposome leakage assays and ATR-FTIR, the authors show that membrane lipid composition and leaflet asymmetry switch the amphipathic CPP MAP between pore-stabilizing insertion/leakage and nondisruptive translocation. Symmetric anionic POPC/POPG bilayers favored pore stabilization, a minimal asymmetric POPC/POPC-POPS model supported translocation without sustained disruption, and cholesterol reduced inserted peptides while accelerating leakage kinetics.

papers.title: JAK Inhibition in Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome: A Case Series from Sydney Children's Hospital.
papers.summary: This case series reports three paediatric FIRES patients treated with the JAK1/2 inhibitor baricitinib alongside immunotherapy, with EEG normalization or improvement and clinically meaningful seizure reduction observed in the patients, although one patient ultimately died.

papers.title: Emergence of ANTI-GAD65 Autoimmunity in Longstanding Drug-Resistant Temporal Lobe Epilepsy.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 29-year-old woman with longstanding drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy in whom high-titre serum and CSF anti-GAD65 antibodies were detected during epilepsy surgery workup, followed by marked seizure reduction after corticosteroids, IVIG, rituximab, and mycophenolate mofetil.

papers.title: [Beyond the ECG-the emotional side of electrophysiology].
papers.summary: This editorial addresses the emotional and human dimensions of electrophysiology practice beyond the electrocardiogram. No abstract or empirical findings were supplied.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
